subject: physics
question_text: A body is projected with a speed u at an angle θ with the horizontal. Obtain expressions for the magnitude and direction of its velocity after a time t.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere. recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The two components
lines: Nothing pushes the body sideways, and
gravity only pulls it down. So

lines.text: v_y = u sin θ − g t

steps.margin_note: First mark. Write both components. The word "unchanged" beside v_x earns it.
steps.why: The horizontal and vertical motions are independent, so each component is handled as a separate straight-line problem.
common_mistakes: Letting g change the horizontal component as well.

recall.must_convey: That v x stays u cos theta and v y is u sin theta minus g t.
accept: u sin theta minus g t
reject: root of v x squared plus v y squared
heard_as: u sin theta minus g t

steps.memory_tip: The horizontal part stays u cos θ for the whole flight. Only the VERTICAL part carries the −gt.

steps.label: The magnitude
lines: The two components are perpendicular, so

lines.text: v = √(u² − 2 u g t sin θ + g²t²)

steps.margin_note: Two marks. Show the expansion and the sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 step, not only the final root.
steps.why: The u² remains because sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 — the same identity that collapses every projectile expression.
common_mistakes: Adding the components directly instead of taking the square root of the sum of squares.

recall.must_convey: That v is the root of v x squared plus v y squared, giving root of u squared minus 2 u g t sin theta plus g squared t squared.
accept: root of v x squared plus v y squared
u squared minus 2 u g t sin theta plus g squared t squared
heard_as: v x squared plus v y squared

steps.memory_tip: Check t = 0: the expression must reduce to v = u. If it does not, the expansion slipped.

steps.label: The direction
lines: If α is the angle of v with the horizontal,
At the top v_y = 0, so α = 0 and v = u cos θ.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Box tan α. The check at the top is worth one more line.
steps.why: The check at the top is worth writing: it shows the body is still moving there, which is the commonest misconception in this chapter.
common_mistakes: Saying the velocity is zero at the top — only its vertical part is.
Reading α as always above the horizontal — after the top, v_y = u sin θ − g t is negative, so tan α is negative and the velocity points below the horizontal.

recall.must_convey: That tan alpha is v y over v x, and at the top v y is zero so v equals u cos theta.
accept: tan alpha is v y by v x
at the top v is u cos theta
reject: root of v x squared plus v y squared

steps.memory_tip: Direction is always tan α = v_y / v_x — the changing part on top, the fixed part below.

insider_note: The magnitude carries 2 of the 4 marks, and the direction is a separate mark — write tan α = v_y / v_x, do not imply it.
